# The upper bound of a ball as a limb, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_upper_as_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An upper bound of the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$, as a number of `T`:

$$h \ge x \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.upper_as<T>()` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `T` | `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `X.upper()` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the same value as a one-limb number; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- If the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is empty: $h = -\infty$.
- Otherwise $h \ge x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line gives $h = +\infty$.
- For a finite ball: $h = \mathrm{RU}(c + r)$, the upper bound of the ball rounded up in the format with overflow.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_upper_as_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_upper_as_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_upper_as_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the center plus the radius, rounded up (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_upper_as_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_upper_as_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

```
# The upper bound of a ball with a one-limb center, as a number of T (milestone2.md, "One
# enclosure interface", the row of lower_as and upper_as, and "The empty set and the whole line"):
# for a finite ball RU(c + r), the smallest number of T not below every member, in the
# format with overflow; the whole line gives +inf (0 + inf rounded up), and the empty ball
# -inf, by the select on the radius, which is a NaN exactly for the empty ball.

t  = add_up_1(c, r)
ne = eq(r, r)
mi = neg(const inf)
h  = select(ne, t, mi)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_upper_as_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 1 961 460 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
